answer: Admission asks for authorship, not stake. Each identity submits a sonnet, an original text whose style embedding is compared with its cluster's, and near-identical embeddings merge into one identity with one shared balance, so a farm of paraphrases collapses into a single plume on the ledger. Stake is willow, flexible in time but not in space: one unit backs one identity at a time, and moving it burns a fee scaling with that stakeholder's k-th move as k squared. Rotating one bond across n heads thus burns nearly n cubed over three and buys nothing, since the merged cluster still counts once.
